- **AC-1** `POST /notes` with body `{"title":"a","body":"b"}` returns status 201 and a JSON note whose `title` is `"a"`, whose `body` is `"b"`, and whose `id` is a positive integer.

- **AC-4** `GET /notes` returns status 200 and a JSON array of every stored note, in creation order. With no notes stored it returns `[]`.

## Context (brownfield)
Existing module `core` (see [docs/wiki/modules/core.md](../wiki/modules/core.md)):
- `src/result.ts` defines `Result<T>`, `ok` and `err`.
- `src/note-store.ts` defines `NoteStore` (`add`, `get`, `list`). Its errors are `'title required'` and `'not found'`.
- `src/search.ts` defines `searchNotes(notes, term)`. Its error is `'term required'`.
- `src/index.ts` re-exports all three.

Conventions kept (from `.daylight/ingest/conventions.md` and the README):
- TypeScript ESM run directly by Node 24, with `.ts` import specifiers
- kebab-case files
- functions never throw and return `Result<T>`
- `node:test` in `tests/`, ESLint (`complexity` 8, `max-lines-per-function` 40), `tsc --noEmit`
- npm

Existing dependency layers stay as they are: `index -> {result, note-store, search}`, `search -> {note-store, result}` and `note-store -> result`.

## New modules (all in `src/`, kebab-case)
| File | Layer | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `src/notes-api.ts` | application (pure) | `handleRequest(store, req: ApiRequest): ApiResult` routes `{method, path, query, body}` through a **route table** to `NoteStore` / `searchNotes`, and returns `Result<T>` values tagged with a route outcome. It never throws and knows nothing about HTTP status codes. |
| `src/http-status.ts` | edge | `toHttpResponse(result): {status, json}` holds the only map from `Result` errors to statuses: `title required`/`term required`/`invalid body` → 400, `not found` → 404, anything else → 500. Success → 200, or 201 for `POST /notes`. |
| `src/request-log.ts` | edge | `formatLogLine(method, pathname, status, ms): string` returns a single line with no body or query string. |
| `src/http-server.ts` | edge | `createServer({store, log})` is a `node:http` adapter. It reads the body (1 MiB cap), parses JSON into a `Result`, calls `handleRequest`, then `toHttpResponse`, then writes the response, then calls `log(formatLogLine(...))`. A top-level `try/catch` at the edge turns any unexpected throw into a 500. |
| `src/main.ts` | entry | Creates a `NoteStore`, calls `createServer({store, log: console.log})` and listens on `PORT` (default 8081). |
| `scripts/smoke.ts` | ops | Uses global `fetch` to run the four checks against `SMOKE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8081`), then `process.exit(0 or 1)`. |
| `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` | deploy | `node:24-alpine` image running `node src/main.ts`. Compose publishes `8081:8081` and has a healthcheck on `/health`. |

Dependency direction: `main -> http-server -> {notes-api, http-status, request-log}` and `notes-api -> {note-store, search, result}`. Nothing in `core` imports the new modules, and `src/index.ts` (the library entry point) stays unchanged so library consumers do not pull in `node:http`.

### ADR-1: Pure route-table handler with status mapping only at the `node:http` edge
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** The PRD requires:
  - library functions never throw and return `Result<T>`
  - HTTP status mapping only at the edge
  - no new runtime dependencies
  - ESLint `complexity` ≤ 8 and `max-lines-per-function` ≤ 40
